clue.text: Means to copy something Atkins banned in theory?

parts.note: the Atkins diet famously cuts out carbohydrates, carbs for short
something true on paper holds in theory but not necessarily in practice

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether the Atkins plan forbids some copying aid, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Atkins diet is a low-carbohydrate regime, so a carb is what it bans.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets coated with ink were laid between pages to make duplicates, so they are a copying device.

clue.text: Ming dynasty, perhaps losing final lines, had temporary place to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ming dynasty' looks Chinese but points to Sir Menzies 'Ming' Campbell, a British Liberal Democrat leader; L is an abbreviation for line.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretched' rearranges the ten letters of ELDORADOVE; 'characters in' just points at those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or circuit with excessive burden heaped on it has been burdened beyond capacity.

clue.text: Sorrow full of meaning after loss of husband

parts.note: pithy remarks are concise and full of meaning

clue.text: Too much god in prayer

explanation.definitionFit: An overabundance or glut is an excessive quantity.

clue.text: Root Mum cooked in anger

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for anger

parts.note: rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Mother has prepared a root vegetable while seething with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' looks like a noun, a vegetable, but here it is the verb meaning to search about; 'cooked' signals the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To root about is to search untidily, which is to forage through things.

clue.text: Barrister's function, getting around judge

explanation.surface: A lawyer's job involves working round the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Rumpole, of the TV series Rumpole of the Bailey, is a famous fictional English barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: John Mortimer's fictional Old Bailey advocate is the best-known example of a barrister in British fiction.

clue.text: Frontless self-assembly unit gentleman set up to hold one's invested money

indicators.note: to hold says the pieces wrap around the letter for one
in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read from bottom to top
frontless means the first letter of the word is removed

sir is a form of address for a gentleman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gentleman builds a flat-pack cabinet without its front panel to store his invested funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frontless' makes LATPACK; 'set up' turns LATPACK + SIR into RISKCAPTAL, and 'to hold' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture funding put into a speculative enterprise, which may be lost, is money invested.

clue.text: Good at insulating room in time to repair

parts.note: to heal is to mend or repair

clue.text: German songs including moving octet which hopes to reveal invention

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' signals the rearranged OCTET; 'invention' in the definition is not a new device but a fabrication, a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph aims to expose falsehood, and invention here means a made-up story.

clue.text: The thing brought in as a hint should be an aid to understanding words

clue.text: Hoax brought to a conclusion

clue.text: Dramatist's country valley edged by Italian river

clue.text: Acquiescent, forgetting son was in control

clue.text: Following this public service would be pointlessness

clue.text: Expose Home Office with due reshuffling
